subject: DeepEval dependency drift: #3064 wrapper carries a stale pre-rebase copy of #3056 alignment

observation: #3056 head ca677d5 contains the corrected 2-D bounded resynchronization search that can advance both traces before rejoining.
#3064 head a0ac51b currently includes its own alignment.py with the older one-sided skew _find_resync implementation, despite the PR body saying it builds on #3056 and does not modify the seam.
Therefore #3064's current wrapper proofs and example scores are bound to an obsolete dependency snapshot and must not be treated as valid against current #3056 semantics.
required_actions: Represent #3064 as a ForeignTwin derived artifact whose validity envelope binds exact dependency head #3056@ca677d5 (or later reviewed equivalent).
Invalidate wrapper result receipts whenever the seam dependency digest changes; do not wait for human prose to notice the drift.

Use DeepEval's own traces as a Replay/Backtesting fixture: execute the same examples against current #3056 seam and current #3064 stale seam, localize result differences, and emit a bounded reconciliation artifact.
Prepare an upstream-ready rebase/reconciliation review draft only; do not post or mutate upstream without authority.
Promote the generic rule into Partner Commons: dependent PR/check evidence is valid only for the exact dependency graph it executed.
body.native_lesson: FactorValidityEnvelope should bind source commit graph, not only tool/version labels. A green dependent artifact becomes stale when an upstream semantic dependency changes even if its own files did not.
